answer.label: Spoken by
answer.authorDates: b. 1971 · CEO of Tesla and SpaceX
answer.sourceLine: Musk said these exact words when Lex Fridman asked what one question he would put to an artificial general intelligence. It came near the end of “Elon Musk: Tesla Autopilot,” an episode of Fridman’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Podcast uploaded April 12, 2019. Quote Investigator ↗ confirms it.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Podcast, hosted by Lex Fridman (now listed on YouTube as Lex Fridman Podcast #18)

source.excerpt:
Lex Fridman: So when, maybe you, or somebody else creates an AGI system, and you get to ask her one question, what would that question be?

(Long pause)

Elon Musk: What’s outside the simulation?
trail: April 12, 2019: Lex Fridman posts the interview “Elon Musk: Tesla Autopilot” (episode page ↗; video ↗). Musk’s answer comes near the end.
April 15, 2019: Inverse ↗ reports that Musk paused for 14 seconds before answering “What’s outside the simulation?”
August 29, 2019: Quote Investigator ↗ traces the line to the Fridman interview and transcribes the exchange, citing the quotation at 31 minutes 57 seconds.
Lex Fridman later posts the exchange as a separate clip, “Elon Musk: What’s Outside the Simulation? | AI Podcast Clips ↗.”

author.name: Elon Musk
author.heading: About Elon Musk
author.metaLine: b. 1971 · Entrepreneur; CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, co-founder of Neuralink
author.bio: Elon Musk leads Tesla and SpaceX and co-founded Neuralink. He is also one of the internet’s favorite targets for made-up quotes. He has argued in public more than once that our reality may be a computer simulation, so this line fits his record and is one of the few viral Musk quotes with a recording behind it.

misattribution.heading: Who gets confused here
misattribution.intro: This Musk line is real, which is rare. The usual mix-ups are about who said which part and what he meant.

items.why: Fridman, then an AI researcher at MIT, asked the question: what one question would Musk put to an AGI system? The answer, “What’s outside the simulation?”, is Musk’s. Quote Investigator ↗ looked at both men and at an apocryphal origin before settling on Musk.

items.who: Elon Musk, quoted as making a claim
items.why: The line is often shared as if Musk were announcing that we live in a simulation. In fact it was his answer to a hypothetical: the one question he would ask an AGI. Quote Investigator ↗ concludes only that Musk suggested he, or humanity, might be in a simulation, and that a future advanced AI might be asked to work out what lies outside it.

misattribution.truthLine: Elon Musk said “What’s outside the simulation?” in Lex Fridman’s interview “Elon Musk: Tesla Autopilot,” uploaded April 12, 2019 (Quote Investigator ↗).

context.heading: Why he asked it
lead: Musk had backed the simulation hypothesis in public before this interview. At Recode’s Code Conference in 2016 he argued that if games keep improving until they are indistinguishable from reality, “the odds that we’re in base reality is one in billions” (as quoted by TechCrunch ↗). He made the case again on The Joe Rogan Experience in 2018 (Wikiquote ↗).

Fridman’s question gave that idea its shortest form. Asked what single question he would put to a human-level AI, Musk passed over questions about physics or the future and asked about the boundary of reality itself.
